name: Bubble chart
reader_question: How do two measures relate across items, and which items carry the most of a third measure?
relationship: Association between two measures with a third, strictly positive magnitude encoded as bubble area.
use_when: A third positive magnitude adds context to a two-measure relationship
Few enough items that each bubble can be named
avoid_when: The size values must be compared precisely — use a ranked bar or a table
Only two measures exist — use scatter
Sizes can be zero or negative

data_contract.notes: Explicit axis range containing every bubble centre
What the area represents and its unit
Two reference sizes for the legend circles, no larger than the largest bubble
Unique items; at most one in the accent

units: Three independent units: x, y and the size measure, each stated on the slide.

editable: Native bubble chart with embedded workbook (Edit Data)
Bubble colours, transparency and axis ranges
not_data_bound: Bubble labels and axis titles are positioned text computed from the fixture
Size-legend reference circles are drawn shapes scaled to PowerPoint's default bubble size (largest bubble = 25% of the shorter plot side); the renderer may differ, so they are approximate

table_alternative: A table of items with x, y and size columns for exact comparison.
variations: Scatter with labelled points when no third measure exists
limitations: Area perception is weak; readers misjudge ratios between bubbles, so exact sizes belong in a table or legend
Large bubbles can hide neighbours, which caps the item count

excluded_alternatives.reason: Depth distorts area and breaks the no-3D rule
Encoding size by radius exaggerates ratios by the square
